questions.question: He and I ______ well.
questions.explanation: When two subjects are joined by "and", the verb is plural. "He and I" → "are".

questions.question: One of the ______ of globalization is cultural ______.
questions.explanation: "One of the" is followed by a plural noun (effects) and a singular verb. First blank = "effects" (plural noun after "one of the").

questions.question: More than one book ___ bought.
questions.explanation: "More than one" + singular noun + singular verb. (More than two → plural noun + plural verb.)

questions.question: A number of banks ___ technology widely.
questions.explanation: "A number of" + plural noun + plural verb. "The number of" + plural noun + singular verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is the correct one?

options.a: Five thousands taka was spent in the function.
options.b: Five thousand taka were spent in the function.
options.c: Five thousands taka were spent in the function.
options.d: Five thousand taka was spent in the function.

questions.correct_answer_text: Five thousand taka was spent in the function.
questions.explanation: Money, time, distance, age treated as a single unit → singular verb. "Thousand" preceded by a number stays singular.

questions.question: The majority of the employees ___ university degrees.
questions.explanation: "Majority of + plural noun" → plural verb. When majority refers to a collection of individuals, use plural verb.

questions.question: Which one is a correct sentence?

options.a: Ten kilometers are too far to walk.
options.b: One should take care of his health.
options.d: The furniture in the living room need to be cleaned regularly.

questions.explanation: When 'each' comes after a plural noun/pronoun, the verb is plural. 'Students each are present' is correct as 'are' agrees with the plural 'Students'.

questions.question: More than one book ___ bought.
questions.explanation: 'More than one + singular noun' takes a singular verb. So 'More than one book is bought' is correct.

questions.question: Either the manager or his assistants ____ the company's personnel needs.
questions.explanation: With 'Either...or', the verb agrees with the closest subject (proximity rule). 'His assistants' (plural) is closest, so 'review' is correct.
